items.meaning: Your voice is becoming unclear or cutting out during a call due to a poor connection.
items.example: I'm sorry, you're breaking up a bit; could you repeat the last part?
items.plain: I can't hear you clearly; please say the last part again.
items.note: Commonly used to politely indicate audio issues on a call. Can be said directly to the person.

items.meaning: Your voice is very quiet or indistinct, making it hard for me to understand what you're saying.
items.example: Could you speak up a little? I can barely hear you over the background noise.
items.plain: Please speak louder; your voice is too quiet for me to hear.
items.note: A direct but polite way to ask someone to increase their volume or clarity on a call.

items.meaning: The phone connection is intermittently failing, causing parts of the conversation to be lost.
items.example: I think we have a bad connection; the line is cutting out every few seconds.
items.plain: Our connection is poor; I keep losing parts of what you're saying.
items.note: Refers specifically to the phone connection itself, often used for mobile or landline calls.

items.meaning: Your video image is temporarily stuck or paused on the screen during a video call.
items.example: Oh, you're freezing on my screen; I think your internet connection might be unstable.
items.plain: Your video is stuck; your internet connection seems to be unstable.
items.note: Used exclusively for video calls when someone's image stops moving due to connection issues.

items.meaning: My internet or phone signal is unreliable, causing interruptions or poor quality during the call.
items.example: Apologies if I drop off, my connection is unstable today due to the bad weather.
items.plain: Sorry if I get disconnected, my internet is not reliable today because of the weather.
items.note: A common and polite way to pre-emptively explain potential technical issues on your end.

items.meaning: Please say again what you just said, as I didn't hear or understand it clearly.
items.example: I missed the last part, could you repeat that for me, please?
items.plain: I didn't hear the end, please say it again.
items.note: A standard, polite request when you've missed something. Very versatile in many contexts.

items.meaning: There is a noticeable pause or lag between when one person speaks and the other hears it.
items.example: Sorry, there's a delay on the line, so I might accidentally talk over you.
items.plain: The sound is lagging, so I might interrupt you by mistake.
items.note: Explains why conversation flow might be awkward, often due to international calls or poor internet.

items.meaning: The sound quality is inconsistent, with parts of the speech cutting in and out rapidly.
items.example: It's hard to follow; the audio is choppy, making your words sound broken.
items.plain: Your sound quality is bad; your words are broken and hard to understand.
items.note: Describes fragmented sound, often due to a weak or intermittent internet connection.

items.meaning: My video feed is not smooth and appears to be behind the audio or real-time actions.
items.example: I'm sorry if I look strange, my video is lagging quite a bit today.
items.plain: My video is delayed, so I might appear odd on screen.
items.note: Indicates a delay in the visual component of a video call, often due to bandwidth issues.

items.meaning: I will attempt to leave and rejoin the call to fix a technical issue.
items.example: The sound is terrible, so let me try reconnecting to see if that helps.
items.plain: The sound is bad, I'll leave and rejoin the call to fix it.
items.note: A proactive statement when you're experiencing technical difficulties and want to fix them.

items.meaning: I'm checking if you are still present and connected to the call after a silence or issue.
items.example: Hello? Are you still there? I haven't heard anything for a moment.
items.plain: Hello? Have you left the call? It's been silent for a moment.
items.note: Used when there's unexpected silence or a suspected disconnection on a call.

items.meaning: Your voice is unclear and indistinct, as if something is covering the microphone.
items.example: Could you adjust your microphone? It sounds a bit muffled.
items.plain: Please fix your microphone; your voice is unclear.
items.note: A polite way to suggest someone's audio quality isn't optimal, often due to mic placement.

items.meaning: I am experiencing difficulty understanding what you are saying due to poor audio.
items.example: I'm having trouble hearing you clearly; the background noise is quite loud.
items.plain: I can't hear you well because of the loud background noise.
items.note: A general phrase to indicate difficulty with audio, can be followed by a specific reason.

items.meaning: Your video image appears blocky and low-resolution due to a poor connection.
items.example: Your video is very blurry; the picture is pixelated on my screen.
items.plain: Your video is blurry and blocky on my screen.
items.note: Describes poor video quality where individual pixels are visible, common with low bandwidth.

items.meaning: I'm asking if my video feed is visible and working correctly on your end.
items.example: I just turned my camera on. Can you see me now?
items.plain: My camera is on. Is my video visible to you?
items.note: Used to confirm video functionality after making an adjustment or joining a call.

items.meaning: I can hear my own voice or other sounds repeating back to me during the call.
items.example: Sorry, I'm getting an echo; could you check your microphone settings?
items.plain: I hear my voice repeating; please check your microphone.
items.note: Indicates an audio feedback loop, often caused by open speakers or multiple microphones.

items.meaning: The audio or video connection is repeatedly failing and restoring, causing interruptions.
items.example: I can't understand you because it keeps cutting out every few words.
items.plain: I can't understand you; the connection is repeatedly failing.
items.note: A common way to describe intermittent connection problems affecting audio or video.

items.meaning: We should end this call and initiate a new one to attempt to fix connection issues.
items.example: The connection is too bad; let's try calling back in a couple of minutes.
items.plain: The connection is poor; we should end this call and start a new one soon.
items.note: A suggestion to restart the call when technical problems are persistent and severe.

items.meaning: The strength of the wireless or cellular connection is low, leading to poor call quality.
items.example: I'm in a rural area, so the signal is weak here, causing poor call quality.
items.plain: I'm in a rural area, so the connection strength is low, making the call quality bad.
items.note: Explains poor call quality due to insufficient network coverage, common for mobile phones.

items.meaning: I would like to politely interrupt the current speaker to add a point or ask a question.
items.example: May I jump in here for a moment? I have a quick question about that.
items.plain: Can I interrupt briefly? I have a quick question.
items.note: A polite way to interject into a conversation, often used in group discussions.

items.meaning: I would like to contribute an additional piece of information or a thought to the discussion.
items.example: If I could just add to what you're saying, I think the timeline is crucial.
items.plain: I'd like to add to your point: the timeline is crucial.
items.note: A polite way to introduce a contribution, often used to build on someone else's point.

items.meaning: To continue discussing or elaborate on a point that someone else has just made.
items.example: To pick up on that point about the budget, we need to consider the long-term costs.
items.plain: Regarding your point about the budget, we must consider long-term costs.
items.note: A useful discourse marker to show you are connecting your statement to a previous one.

items.meaning: Please allow me to complete my current thought or statement without interruption.
items.example: I understand your concern, but let me just finish explaining the process first.
items.plain: I know your concern, but please let me complete my explanation first.
items.note: A firm but polite way to regain the floor when someone is interrupting you.

items.meaning: An apology for breaking into someone else's speech, used before making your own point.
items.example: Sorry to interrupt, but I have a conflicting appointment at that time.
items.plain: My apologies for interrupting, but I have another appointment then.
items.note: A standard polite apology when you need to interject, showing respect for the other speaker.

items.meaning: An invitation for someone to speak or continue speaking, often after a pause or interruption.
items.example: You looked like you wanted to say something, so please, go ahead.
items.plain: You seemed to want to speak, so please, start talking.
items.note: A common and informal way to give someone permission to speak or proceed.

items.meaning: I'm asking for your opinion or perspective on the topic being discussed.
items.example: We've discussed my proposal; now, what are your thoughts on the implementation?
items.plain: I've presented my idea; what do you think about implementing it?
items.note: A direct and inclusive way to invite others to contribute to the conversation.

items.meaning: I'm asking if you have anything further to contribute to the current discussion.
items.example: Before we move on, did you want to add anything to that point?
items.plain: Before we continue, do you have anything else to say about that?
items.note: A polite way to check if someone has more to say, ensuring everyone has a chance to speak.

items.meaning: I wish to politely interrupt the conversation to make a point or ask a question.
items.example: If I may, I'd like to interject a quick question about the budget figures.
items.plain: If I may, I want to interrupt with a quick question about the budget.
items.note: A more formal way to interrupt than 'jump in', suitable for professional settings.

items.meaning: Please let me explain something more clearly or provide additional detail.
items.example: I think there's a misunderstanding, so allow me to clarify my previous statement.
items.plain: I believe there's a misunderstanding, so let me explain my last point better.
items.note: Used when you perceive confusion or want to ensure your message is understood precisely.

items.meaning: I want to ensure that a specific point is fully understood and unambiguous.
items.example: Just to be clear, we're meeting at 10 AM tomorrow, not 11 AM, correct?
items.plain: To confirm, our meeting is at 10 AM tomorrow, not 11 AM, right?
items.note: A common discourse marker used to confirm understanding or correct a potential misunderstanding.

items.meaning: I will express what I just said in different words to make it clearer or more accurate.
items.example: That didn't come out right; let me rephrase that to avoid confusion.
items.plain: I didn't say that well; I'll say it differently to be clearer.
items.note: Used when you feel your previous statement was unclear, poorly worded, or misunderstood.

items.meaning: I don't fully understand what you are saying or the point you are trying to make.
items.example: Could you explain that again? I'm not sure I follow your logic.
items.plain: Can you explain that again? I don't understand your reasoning.
items.note: A polite way to admit confusion and ask for further explanation without sounding critical.

items.meaning: Please provide more details or further explanation on a particular point.
items.example: That's an interesting idea; could you elaborate on how it would work?
items.plain: That's interesting; can you give more details on how it would function?
items.note: A polite and professional request for more information or a deeper explanation.

items.meaning: I understand your point of view, even if I don't necessarily agree with it.
items.example: I hear what you're saying about the risks, but I think the benefits outweigh them.
items.plain: I understand your point about the risks, but I believe the benefits are greater.
items.note: A softening phrase, acknowledging the other person's perspective before presenting a different one.

items.meaning: To return to a previous topic or point that was discussed earlier in the conversation.
items.example: To circle back to our earlier discussion, have you had a chance to review the report?
items.plain: Returning to our earlier discussion, have you reviewed the report yet?
items.note: A useful discourse marker for revisiting a topic, ensuring all points are covered.

items.meaning: I'm asking to be reminded of the point I was making before an interruption or digression.
items.example: Sorry, I got sidetracked. Where was I before the phone rang?
items.plain: Apologies, I lost my train of thought. What was I saying before the call?
items.note: A common informal phrase used to get back on track after an interruption.

items.meaning: To resume a point or explanation after an interruption or brief pause.
items.example: As I was saying before the connection dropped, the project deadline is next Friday.
items.plain: Before the call disconnected, I was explaining that the project deadline is next Friday.
items.note: Used to smoothly transition back to your original point after an interruption.

items.meaning: I want to confirm my understanding of the situation or details to ensure accuracy.
items.example: So, let me get this straight: we're postponing the meeting until next week?
items.plain: So, I want to confirm: the meeting is postponed until next week?
items.note: Used to summarise or rephrase information to ensure correct understanding, often before agreeing.

items.meaning: I have a specific point or comment that I wish to express.
items.example: Before we finish, I just wanted to say thank you for your help.
items.plain: Before we finish, I want to express my gratitude for your help.
items.note: A common, polite way to introduce a brief comment or express appreciation.

items.meaning: I want to ensure all current points are covered before proceeding to the next topic.
items.example: Before we move on to the next agenda item, does anyone have further questions?
items.plain: Does anyone have more questions before we discuss the next topic?
items.note: A useful phrase for managing the flow of a meeting or structured conversation.

items.meaning: I'm asking if you need clarification or further information on what has been discussed.
items.example: I've explained the new policy; do you have any questions about it?
items.plain: I've explained the new policy; do you need more information?
items.note: A standard closing question after presenting information, inviting engagement.

items.meaning: I will transfer the responsibility for speaking or leading the discussion to another person.
items.example: That concludes my update, so I'll hand it over to Sarah for her report.
items.plain: My update is done, so Sarah will now present her report.
items.note: Common in meetings or presentations to smoothly transition between speakers.

items.meaning: I will provide background information necessary to understand the current situation or topic.
items.example: To give you some context, we've been working on this project for six months.
items.plain: For background information, we started this project half a year ago.
items.note: Used to provide necessary background information before diving into details.

items.text: let me put it another way
items.form: Let me put it another way
items.meaning: I will explain something again using different words to make it clearer.
items.example: Perhaps that wasn't clear; let me put it another way to ensure understanding.
items.plain: That might not have been clear; I'll explain it differently so you understand.
items.note: Used when you suspect your initial explanation wasn't fully grasped.

items.meaning: I understand what you've said up to this point in your explanation.
items.example: Yes, I'm with you so far; please continue with the next step.
items.plain: Yes, I understand what you've said; please explain the next step.
items.note: A useful phrase to indicate comprehension and encourage the speaker to proceed.

items.meaning: Please explain that in very clear, simple terms, or literally spell a word.
items.example: I'm not familiar with that acronym; could you spell that out for me?
items.plain: I don't know that acronym; can you explain it clearly?
items.note: Can mean to explain simply or to literally spell a word. Context clarifies.

items.meaning: I'm starting to find it difficult to follow your explanation or the conversation.
items.example: The technical details are getting complex; I'm losing you a bit.
items.plain: The technical details are complex; I'm starting to not understand.
items.note: A polite way to indicate you're struggling to keep up with the conversation's complexity.

items.meaning: I want to confirm if I have correctly understood what you have said.
items.example: Before we proceed, let me check my understanding of the next steps.
items.plain: Before we continue, I want to confirm I understand the next steps.
items.note: A professional way to ensure accuracy and avoid miscommunication.

items.meaning: I want to verify a piece of information to ensure it is correct.
items.example: Just to confirm, the meeting is indeed at 3 PM, not 2 PM, right?
items.plain: I want to verify, the meeting is at 3 PM, not 2 PM, correct?
items.note: A common phrase used to double-check details, often at the end of a discussion.

items.meaning: To bring the conversation or meeting to a close by summarising or concluding.
items.example: Okay, to wrap things up, let's agree on these three action points.
items.plain: Alright, to finish, let's agree on these three action points.
items.note: A very common and natural way to signal the end of a discussion or meeting.

items.meaning: Let's stop working or end the meeting for today.
items.example: We've made good progress, so let's call it a day and pick this up tomorrow.
items.plain: We've done well, so let's stop working now and continue tomorrow.
items.note: An informal but widely accepted phrase to end work or a meeting for the day.

items.meaning: I need to leave now because I have another commitment or need to go somewhere.
items.example: It's been great talking, but I need to run to my next appointment.
items.plain: It was good talking, but I must leave for my next appointment.
items.note: A common, informal way to politely excuse yourself from a call or meeting.

items.meaning: I am ending the call, giving you permission to disconnect.
items.example: I know you're busy, so I'll let you go now. Thanks for your time.
items.plain: I know you're busy, so I'm ending the call. Thank you for your time.
items.note: A polite way to end a call, implying you are considerate of the other person's time.

items.meaning: An expression of gratitude to the person who initiated the phone call.
items.example: It was good to catch up. Thanks for calling!
items.plain: It was good to talk. I appreciate you calling!
items.note: A standard, polite closing phrase when ending a call, especially if you were called.

items.meaning: A polite closing remark, expressing enjoyment or satisfaction with the conversation.
items.example: Well, it was good to talk to you. I'll be in touch soon.
items.plain: It was nice speaking with you. I'll contact you shortly.
items.note: A common, friendly way to end a conversation, suitable for both formal and informal calls.

items.meaning: We have discussed many topics or a significant amount of information during our conversation.
items.example: I think we've covered a lot today, so let's aim to meet again next week.
items.plain: We discussed many things today, so let's plan to meet again next week.
items.note: Used to acknowledge the breadth of discussion, often as a lead-in to wrapping up.

items.meaning: I will briefly restate the main points and conclusions of our conversation.
items.example: To summarise our discussion, we'll proceed with option A and review it next month.
items.plain: In summary, we'll go with option A and check it again next month.
items.note: A formal and clear way to recap key outcomes at the end of a meeting or call.

items.meaning: I believe we have completed our business or discussion for this call/meeting.
items.example: Unless anyone has anything else, I think we're done here.
items.plain: If there's nothing else, I believe our discussion is complete.
items.note: A direct way to signal the end of a discussion, inviting final comments.

items.meaning: I will contact you again later to provide more information or check on progress.
items.example: I'll follow up with an email containing all the details we discussed.
items.plain: I will send an email later with all the details we talked about.
items.note: A common professional phrase to indicate future communication or action.

items.meaning: Let's communicate briefly again in the near future to update each other or discuss progress.
items.example: We've made a plan, so let's touch base soon to see how things are progressing.
items.plain: We have a plan, so let's talk briefly again soon to check progress.
items.note: An informal but professional way to suggest a future brief check-in call or message.

items.meaning: I will compose and transmit an electronic message to you or someone else.
items.example: I'll send an email with the meeting minutes and action items by the end of the day.
items.plain: I will email the meeting notes and tasks by the end of today.
items.note: A straightforward statement of intent to communicate via email, often for summaries or actions.

items.meaning: I'm asking if there are any other topics or points that need to be discussed.
items.example: We've covered the main points. Is there anything else we need to address?
items.plain: We've discussed the main topics. Do we need to talk about anything else?
items.note: A standard closing question to ensure all matters have been addressed before ending.

items.meaning: I will contact you again later, usually with an answer or more information.
items.example: I don't have that information right now, but I'll get back to you by tomorrow.
items.plain: I don't have that information now, but I will contact you by tomorrow.
items.note: A very common and useful phrase for promising a future response or contact.

items.meaning: We have very little time left to complete our discussion or meeting.
items.example: We're running out of time, so let's quickly decide on the next steps.
items.plain: We have little time left, so let's quickly decide on the next actions.
items.note: Used to gently urge a group to conclude or make decisions due to time constraints.

items.meaning: I will regularly update you with new information as it becomes available.
items.example: The situation is still developing, but I'll keep you posted on any changes.
items.plain: The situation is changing, but I will inform you of any updates.
items.note: A friendly and reassuring way to promise ongoing updates, often for evolving situations.

items.meaning: The phone call or video conference has achieved its goals and yielded good results.
items.example: Thank you for your input; it's been a productive call, and we've made good decisions.
items.plain: Thanks for your input; the call was fruitful, and we made good decisions.
items.note: A positive closing remark, indicating that the time spent on the call was worthwhile.

items.meaning: I am grateful for the time you have spent speaking with me or attending this meeting.
items.example: Thank you for joining; I appreciate your time and valuable insights.
items.plain: Thanks for joining; I'm grateful for your time and helpful insights.
items.note: A formal and polite expression of gratitude, especially at the end of a professional interaction.

items.meaning: We should arrange a future phone or video conversation to continue our discussion.
items.example: We couldn't cover everything, so let's schedule another call for next week.
items.plain: We didn't finish everything, so let's arrange another call next week.
items.note: A common way to propose a follow-up conversation when more discussion is needed.

items.meaning: I will transmit the written summary or record of our discussion to you.
items.example: I'll send over the notes from our meeting later today for everyone's reference.
items.plain: I will email the meeting summary later today for everyone to review.
items.note: A professional way to promise to share meeting minutes or a summary of discussion points.

items.meaning: To briefly summarise the main points that have been discussed.
items.example: To recap quickly, we've agreed on the budget and the project timeline.
items.plain: To summarise briefly, we've agreed on the budget and project timeline.
items.note: Used to provide a brief summary, often before moving to the next topic or ending the call.

items.meaning: I believe all necessary topics have been covered and there's nothing more to discuss.
items.example: Unless anyone has anything else, I think that's everything for today's meeting.
items.plain: If no one has more to add, I believe we've finished for today's meeting.
items.note: A common way to signal the end of a discussion, inviting final contributions.

items.meaning: I will contact you again in the near future.
items.example: I'll review the documents and then I'll be in touch with my feedback.
items.plain: I will check the documents and then contact you with my comments.
items.note: A general and polite way to promise future communication, without specifying how or when.

items.meaning: A friendly, informal way to wish someone a good day, evening, or weekend.
items.example: Alright, I'll talk to you next week. Have a good one!
items.plain: Okay, I'll speak to you next week. Have a good day!
items.note: A very common and casual closing remark, suitable for most informal and semi-formal interactions.

items.meaning: I will stop discussing this topic or end my contribution to the conversation.
items.example: I think I've made my point, so I'll leave it there for now.
items.plain: I believe I've explained my point, so I'll stop talking about it for now.
items.note: Used to signal that you've finished your contribution to a topic, often after making a strong point.

items.meaning: I am making this phone call to discuss or inquire about a specific subject.
items.example: Hello, I'm calling about the job application I submitted last week.
items.plain: Hello, I'm calling regarding the job application I sent last week.
items.note: A standard and direct way to state the purpose of your call at the beginning.

items.meaning: I am requesting that you return my phone call at your convenience.
items.example: I'm unavailable right now, so please call me back when you have a moment.
items.plain: I'm busy now, so please return my call when you are free.
items.note: A common request left on voicemails or in messages when you can't speak immediately.

items.meaning: I will record a voicemail or write a note for the person I am trying to reach.
items.example: Since you're not available, I'll leave a message explaining my query.
items.plain: As you're busy, I will record a voicemail explaining my question.
items.note: Used when someone is unavailable, indicating you will provide information for them to retrieve.

items.meaning: I am calling you back in response to a previous call you made to me.
items.example: Hi John, I'm returning your call about the project update.
items.plain: Hi John, I'm calling you back about the project update.
items.note: A standard opening phrase when you are calling someone back who previously called you.

items.meaning: An apology for not being available to answer your phone call when you rang.
items.example: Sorry I missed your call earlier; I was in a meeting.
items.plain: My apologies for not answering your call earlier; I was in a meeting.
items.note: A polite apology when you call someone back after they tried to reach you.

items.text: I'll get back to you shortly
items.form: I'll get back to you shortly
items.meaning: I will contact you again very soon, usually within a short period of time.
items.example: I need to check my calendar, but I'll get back to you shortly with my availability.
items.plain: I need to check my schedule, but I will contact you very soon with my availability.
items.note: A common professional phrase promising a quick response, often used in voicemails or emails.

items.meaning: I am currently not able to take your call or speak with you.
items.example: I'm unavailable right now, but please leave a message after the tone.
items.plain: I cannot speak at this moment, but please leave a message.
items.note: A standard phrase used in voicemail greetings or automated responses.

items.meaning: You can contact me using the following phone number or email address.
items.example: If you have any further questions, you can reach me at my office number.
items.plain: If you have more questions, you can contact me using my office number.
items.note: A common way to provide contact information, often at the end of a message.

items.meaning: I will attempt to call or contact you at a subsequent time.
items.example: You're busy now, so I'll try again later this afternoon.
items.plain: You're busy now, so I will attempt to call you again this afternoon.
items.note: Used when someone is unavailable, indicating you will make another attempt to connect.

items.meaning: I am contacting you again to check on the status of a previous matter or conversation.
items.example: Hi, I'm just following up on the email I sent regarding the project proposal.
items.plain: Hello, I'm contacting you again about the project proposal email I sent.
items.note: A common and polite way to initiate a call or message about an ongoing issue.

items.meaning: Please record a voicemail or write a note for the person you are trying to contact.
items.example: He's not at his desk; could you leave a message for him?
items.plain: He's not here; can you record a message for him?
items.note: A polite request from a receptionist or assistant when someone is unavailable.

items.meaning: I will relay the information you've given me to the intended recipient.
items.example: He's in a meeting, but I'll pass on your message as soon as he's free.
items.plain: He's in a meeting, but I will give him your message when he's available.
items.note: Used by an intermediary to assure the caller that their information will be delivered.

items.meaning: I will contact you again in the near future, typically within a short timeframe.
items.example: I need to gather some information, but I'll be in touch soon with an update.
items.plain: I need to get some information, but I will contact you shortly with an update.
items.note: A common and reassuring phrase to promise future communication, often in a professional context.

items.meaning: I will call you on the phone.
items.example: I'll check my schedule and then I'll give you a ring to confirm our meeting time.
items.plain: I will check my schedule and then call you to confirm our meeting time.
items.note: An informal, friendly way to say 'I'll call you', common in British English.

items.meaning: I will send you a brief message, usually an email or text.
items.example: I'll confirm the details by email; I'll drop you a line later today.
items.plain: I will confirm the details by email; I'll send you a short message later today.
items.note: An informal, slightly old-fashioned but still used phrase for sending a short written message.

items.meaning: I will send you a short message via SMS or a messaging app.
items.example: I'll send you a text with the address and directions to the restaurant.
items.plain: I will send you an SMS with the restaurant's address and directions.
items.note: A direct and common way to promise to send a text message.

items.text: I'll get back to you by
items.form: I'll get back to you by
items.meaning: I will contact you again no later than a specified time or date.
items.example: I need to consult with my team, but I'll get back to you by Friday with an answer.
items.plain: I need to talk to my team, but I will contact you by Friday with an answer.
items.note: A professional way to set an expectation for when a response will be provided.

items.meaning: I am making this call specifically to verify a detail or arrangement.
items.example: Hi, I'm calling to confirm our appointment for tomorrow morning.
items.plain: Hello, I'm calling to verify our appointment for tomorrow morning.
items.note: A clear and concise way to state the purpose of a call, often for appointments or bookings.

items.meaning: I am making this phone call in relation to a specific subject or issue.
items.example: Good morning, I'm calling regarding the invoice for last month's services.
items.plain: Good morning, I'm calling about the invoice for last month's services.
items.note: A slightly more formal alternative to 'I'm calling about', suitable for professional contexts.

items.meaning: I will be free to speak or meet starting at a particular time.
items.example: I have a meeting until 2 PM, so I'll be available from 2:30 PM onwards.
items.plain: I have a meeting until 2 PM, so I will be free to talk from 2:30 PM.
items.note: Used to specify your availability for a call or meeting, often in messages.

items.meaning: I will look at my schedule to determine my availability for a meeting or call.
items.example: That sounds good, but I'll check my calendar first to confirm my availability.
items.plain: That sounds good, but I will look at my schedule first to confirm if I'm free.
items.note: A common phrase used to indicate you need to verify your schedule before committing.

items.text: I'll get back to you on that
items.form: I'll get back to you on that
items.meaning: I will provide you with an answer or information regarding that specific point later.
items.example: I don't have the exact figures now, but I'll get back to you on that by tomorrow.
items.plain: I don't have the exact numbers now, but I will give you that information by tomorrow.
items.note: Used to defer a specific question or request, promising a future response.

items.meaning: I will contact you by phone.
items.example: Once I have the updated report, I'll give you a call to discuss it.
items.plain: After I have the updated report, I will phone you to discuss it.
items.note: A standard and common way to say you will phone someone.

items.meaning: I will contact you, usually to communicate or ask for something.
items.example: I'll gather the necessary information and then I'll reach out to you next week.
items.plain: I will collect the information and then contact you next week.
items.note: A professional and slightly formal way to say 'I'll contact you', often used in business.

items.meaning: I will watch or look carefully for something you mentioned or are expecting.
items.example: Thanks for sending the document; I'll keep an eye out for it in my inbox.
items.plain: Thanks for sending the document; I will watch for it in my inbox.
items.note: A common phrase to confirm you will be vigilant for an incoming message or item.

items.meaning: I am making this call to ask for information about a specific topic.
items.example: Good afternoon, I'm calling to inquire about the status of my recent order.
items.plain: Good afternoon, I'm calling to ask about the status of my recent order.
items.note: A formal and polite way to state the purpose of a call when seeking information.

items.meaning: I am contacting you briefly to see how things are going or for a quick update.
items.example: Hi, I'm just checking in to see if you received my previous email.
items.plain: Hello, I'm contacting you briefly to see if you got my last email.
items.note: A casual and friendly way to initiate contact, often without a specific urgent agenda.

items.meaning: I will send or deliver the specified item or information to you.
items.example: I'll get that to you by the end of the day, along with the other documents.
items.plain: I will send that to you by the end of the day, with the other documents.
items.note: A common phrase to promise delivery of a document, file, or piece of information.

items.meaning: I will definitely perform a specific action or ensure something happens.
items.example: Thanks for the reminder; I'll be sure to include that point in the report.
items.plain: Thanks for the reminder; I will definitely include that point in the report.
items.note: Used to give a strong assurance that an action will be taken.

items.text: I'll make a note of that
items.form: I'll make a note of that
items.meaning: I will write down the information you've provided so I don't forget it.
items.example: That's an important detail; I'll make a note of that for the meeting.
items.plain: That's important; I will write it down for the meeting.
items.note: A common phrase to confirm you've registered important information.

items.meaning: I will remember what you've said and consider it in future decisions or actions.
items.example: Thanks for your suggestion; I'll keep that in mind when planning the next phase.
items.plain: Thanks for your idea; I will remember it when planning the next phase.
items.note: A polite way to acknowledge advice or information, implying future consideration.

items.meaning: I will investigate or research the matter you've raised.
items.example: That's a valid concern; I'll look into it and get back to you with a solution.
items.plain: That's a valid concern; I will investigate it and contact you with a solution.
items.note: A common phrase to promise investigation or research into a problem or question.

items.meaning: I will start working on that task or issue immediately.
items.example: Thanks for letting me know; I'll get right on that and send you an update soon.
items.plain: Thanks for informing me; I will start working on it immediately and update you.
items.note: An informal but common phrase to indicate immediate action will be taken.

items.meaning: I am willing and pleased to assist you with your request.
items.example: If you need assistance with the report, I'll be happy to help.
items.plain: If you need help with the report, I am pleased to assist you.
items.note: A polite and enthusiastic way to offer assistance, often in response to a request.

items.meaning: I will ensure that a specific action is carried out or a condition is met.
items.example: I'll make sure to send the updated figures before the end of the day.
items.plain: I will ensure that the updated figures are sent before the end of the day.
items.note: A strong commitment to perform an action, indicating reliability.

items.meaning: I will verify details or arrangements with you to ensure accuracy.
items.example: I'll confirm with you the exact time of the meeting once it's set.
items.plain: I will verify the exact meeting time with you once it's decided.
items.note: A professional way to promise to verify information with someone directly.

items.meaning: I will inform you about something as soon as I have the information.
items.example: I'm waiting for approval, but I'll let you know the decision as soon as possible.
items.plain: I'm waiting for approval, but I will inform you of the decision quickly.
items.note: A very common and versatile phrase to promise to share information.

items.text: I'll get back to my desk
items.form: I'll get back to my desk
items.meaning: I will return to my workspace to continue working or access resources.
items.example: I'm away from my computer, but I'll get back to my desk and send that file.
items.plain: I'm not at my computer, but I will return to my workspace and send the file.
items.note: Used to explain a delay in providing information or taking action, implying you're mobile.

items.text: I'll be sure to pass that on
items.form: I'll be sure to pass that on
items.meaning: I will definitely relay the information you've given me to the correct person.
items.example: Thanks for the feedback; I'll be sure to pass that on to the development team.
items.plain: Thanks for the feedback; I will definitely give it to the development team.
items.note: A strong assurance that a message or feedback will be delivered to the intended recipient.

items.meaning: I will contact you again very soon.
items.example: I need a moment to review this, but I'll be in touch shortly with my thoughts.
items.plain: I need a moment to review this, but I will contact you very soon with my thoughts.
items.note: A professional and polite way to promise a quick follow-up communication.

items.meaning: I will provide you with the latest information or progress report.
items.example: The team is working on it, and I'll send you an update by the end of the day.
items.plain: The team is working on it, and I will send you the latest information today.
items.note: A common phrase to promise a progress report or new information.

items.meaning: I will provide you with advance notice or a warning about something.
items.example: If there are any changes to the schedule, I'll give you a heads-up immediately.
items.plain: If the schedule changes, I will inform you immediately.
items.note: An informal but common phrase for providing advance notice, often about potential issues.

items.text: I'll be sure to follow up
items.form: I'll be sure to follow up
items.meaning: I will definitely contact you again to check on progress or provide more information.
items.example: Thanks for the information; I'll be sure to follow up with the relevant department.
items.plain: Thanks for the information; I will definitely contact the relevant department.
items.note: A strong commitment to ensure a follow-up action is taken, often in a professional context.

items.meaning: Asking if the other person's audio reception is good.
items.example: Hello? Can you hear me clearly, or is the connection still bad?
items.plain: Hello? Is my sound clear to you, or is the connection still bad?
items.note: A polite way to check audio quality at the start or during a call.

items.meaning: Explaining that there's unwanted noise or disruption on the line.
items.example: I'm experiencing some interference on my end; it's making it hard to focus.
items.plain: There's some noise on my line, making it hard to focus.
items.note: Formal and polite, used to describe technical audio issues.

items.meaning: Describing a crackling or hissing sound on the call.
items.example: I'm sorry, but there's a lot of static on your line, making it difficult to understand.
items.plain: Your line has a lot of crackling noise, so it's hard to understand.
items.note: Common phrase for poor audio quality, usually due to a weak signal.

items.meaning: Indicating difficulty understanding what someone is saying due to poor audio.
items.example: I can't quite make out what you're saying; the sound is very faint.
items.plain: I can't understand what you're saying because the sound is very faint.
items.note: A polite way to express difficulty hearing or understanding.

items.meaning: Describing a video feed that is not smooth and appears to skip frames.
items.example: The image is very jumpy on your video feed, so I can't see you clearly.
items.plain: Your video is skipping frames, so I can't see you clearly.
items.note: Used to describe poor video quality, often due to low bandwidth.

items.text: I'm getting a lot of background noise
items.form: I'm getting a lot of background noise
items.meaning: Informing someone that there's distracting sound coming from their environment.
items.example: I'm getting a lot of background noise from your side; could you mute for a moment?
items.plain: There's a lot of noise from your location; could you mute for a moment?
items.note: A polite request to manage ambient sound during a call.

items.text: Could you speak up a little
items.form: Could you speak up a little
items.meaning: Politely asking someone to increase their volume.
items.example: I'm having trouble hearing you; could you speak up a little, please?
items.plain: I can't hear you well; please speak louder.
items.note: A common and polite request when the other person's volume is too low.

items.meaning: Explaining that one is struggling to establish or maintain a call.
items.example: I'm having difficulty connecting to the meeting; it keeps timing out.
items.plain: I'm struggling to join the meeting because it keeps timing out.
items.note: A general phrase for technical issues preventing a call from starting.

items.meaning: Informing others that one's audio input device is malfunctioning.
items.example: I apologize, my microphone isn't working, so I'll have to type in the chat.
items.plain: My microphone is broken, so I'll have to type in the chat.
items.note: A direct way to explain why you can't speak on a call.

items.text: I think my camera is off
items.form: I think my camera is off
items.meaning: Stating that one's video output device might not be active.
items.example: I think my camera is off; can you see me on your screen?
items.plain: My camera might not be on; can you see me?
items.note: Used when unsure if your video is transmitting.

items.meaning: Suggesting to end the current call and initiate a new one to fix issues.
items.example: The audio is really bad; let me restart the call and see if that helps.
items.plain: The audio is terrible; I'll end and begin the call again to see if it improves.
items.note: A common solution for persistent connection problems.

items.text: I'll try calling from my phone
items.form: I'll try calling from my phone
items.meaning: Suggesting to switch devices for the call, often due to computer issues.
items.example: My laptop connection is poor, so I'll try calling from my phone instead.
items.plain: My laptop's internet is bad, so I'll use my phone to call.
items.note: A practical solution when one device has better connectivity.

items.meaning: Describing the sound on the call as low fidelity or unclear.
items.example: I'm afraid the audio quality is poor, making it hard to catch every word.
items.plain: The sound is bad, so it's hard to hear every word.
items.note: A general statement about bad sound, often used in formal contexts.

items.meaning: Informing that one cannot hear anything from the other participant.
items.example: Hello? I'm not getting any sound from your side at all.
items.plain: Hello? I can't hear anything from you.
items.note: A direct way to state a complete lack of audio.

items.meaning: Describing a video stream that is not smooth and appears to stutter.
items.example: The video feed is choppy, so it's hard to follow your presentation slides.
items.plain: Your video is not smooth, making it hard to follow your presentation.
items.note: Similar to "jumpy," but often implies more frequent, smaller interruptions.

items.meaning: Explaining that one's internet connection is problematic.
items.example: I'm having network issues today, so please bear with me if I drop off.
items.plain: My internet connection is bad today, so please be patient if I disconnect.
items.note: A common and professional way to explain connectivity problems.

items.meaning: Informally stating that one's internet connection is not working correctly.
items.example: My internet is acting up, so I might need to rejoin the call.
items.plain: My internet is not working well, so I might need to rejoin.
items.note: More informal than "network issues," but still acceptable in many professional settings.

items.text: I'll switch to a different network
items.form: I'll switch to a different network
items.meaning: Stating an intention to change internet connections to improve stability.
items.example: This Wi-Fi isn't working; I'll switch to a different network to improve the call.
items.plain: This Wi-Fi is bad; I'll change internet connections to make the call better.
items.note: A proactive step to resolve connectivity problems.

items.meaning: Introducing a re-explanation of something previously said.
items.example: To clarify my point, I meant we should prioritize the first two tasks.
items.plain: I want to explain my idea more clearly: we should prioritize the first two tasks.
items.note: Used when you feel your previous statement might have been misunderstood.

items.text: What I mean to say is
items.form: What I mean to say is
items.meaning: Introducing a rephrasing or further explanation of one's thoughts.
items.example: What I mean to say is that the budget constraints are tighter than expected.
items.plain: The budget constraints are tighter than expected.
items.note: A common frame to elaborate or correct a previous statement.

items.meaning: Politely asking for more details or information about a topic.
items.example: That's an interesting idea; could you expand on that a little more?
items.plain: That's interesting; could you give more details about it?
items.note: A polite way to invite someone to elaborate.

items.meaning: Introducing one's interpretation of a situation or information.
items.example: My understanding is that we need to submit the report by Friday.
items.plain: I believe we need to submit the report by Friday.
items.note: Used to state your current grasp of a situation, often seeking confirmation.

items.meaning: A polite way to acknowledge that one's previous statement might have been unclear.
items.example: Perhaps I didn't explain myself clearly; let me try another approach.
items.plain: Maybe I wasn't clear; I'll try to explain it differently.
items.note: A diplomatic way to take responsibility for a communication breakdown.

items.text: I wanted to follow up on
items.form: I wanted to follow up on
items.meaning: Introducing a return to a previous topic or action point.
items.example: I wanted to follow up on the discussion we had about the new project.
items.plain: I wanted to revisit our discussion about the new project.
items.note: Used to bring attention back to a specific item from a past conversation.

items.meaning: Politely asking for an illustration to clarify a point.
items.example: I'm not quite grasping the concept; could you give an example?
items.plain: I don't understand the concept; can you provide an example?
items.note: A common request for clarification, especially for abstract ideas.

items.meaning: Expressing partial confusion or a need for more information about something.
items.example: I'm not entirely clear on the next steps for the implementation phase.
items.plain: I don't fully understand the next steps for the implementation phase.
items.note: A polite and professional way to admit a lack of full understanding.

items.meaning: Introducing a more detailed explanation of a point.
items.example: To elaborate a little, our team has identified several potential risks.
items.plain: To give more details, our team has identified several potential risks.
items.note: Used when you want to add more information to what you've just said.

items.meaning: Acknowledging that one understands the other person's perspective.
items.example: I see your point about the timeline, but we still need to meet the deadline.
items.plain: I understand your perspective on the timeline, but we still need to meet the deadline.
items.note: A common phrase to show understanding, even if you don't fully agree.

items.text: I'd like to offer a perspective
items.form: I'd like to offer a perspective
items.meaning: Politely introducing one's own viewpoint on a matter.
items.example: If I may, I'd like to offer a perspective on the budget allocation.
items.plain: If I may, I want to share my view on the budget allocation.
items.note: A formal and polite way to contribute to a discussion.

items.meaning: A polite way to ask for permission to speak or add a remark.
items.example: If I may just comment, I think we should consider the long-term implications.
items.plain: May I add a comment? I think we should consider the long-term implications.
items.note: A formal and deferential way to interject.

items.meaning: Asking for someone's opinion or viewpoint on a specific issue.
items.example: We've discussed my ideas, but what's your take on this proposal?
items.plain: We've discussed my ideas, but what do you think about this proposal?
items.note: An informal but common way to solicit opinions.

items.text: I'm keen to hear your thoughts
items.form: I'm keen to hear your thoughts
items.meaning: Expressing eagerness to listen to someone's opinions or ideas.
items.example: Before we decide, I'm keen to hear your thoughts on the new strategy.
items.plain: Before we decide, I really want to hear your opinions on the new strategy.
items.note: A polite and engaging way to invite contributions.

items.meaning: Introducing a restatement of one's stance or opinion.
items.example: To reiterate my position, I believe we should proceed with caution.
items.plain: To repeat my stance, I believe we should proceed with caution.
items.note: Used to emphasize or clarify a previously stated viewpoint.

items.meaning: Emphasizing the importance of a particular point.
items.example: I'd like to underscore that client satisfaction is our top priority.
items.plain: I want to emphasize that client satisfaction is our top priority.
items.note: A formal way to highlight the significance of something.

items.meaning: Asking someone to explain a process or concept step-by-step.
items.example: I'm new to this system; could you walk me through the setup process?
items.plain: I'm new to this system; can you explain the setup process step-by-step?
items.note: A polite request for a detailed, guided explanation.

items.meaning: Expressing that one is making an effort to understand something complex.
items.example: I'm trying to grasp the implications of these new regulations.
items.plain: I'm trying to understand the implications of these new regulations.
items.note: Shows active engagement in understanding a difficult topic.

items.meaning: Introducing the primary worry or issue one has.
items.example: My main concern is how this will affect our existing customers.
items.plain: My biggest worry is how this will affect our existing customers.
items.note: A direct way to state your primary reservation or worry.

items.meaning: Introducing one's personal opinion or interpretation of a situation.
items.example: The way I see it, we have two viable options moving forward.
items.plain: In my opinion, we have two good options moving forward.
items.note: A common, slightly informal frame to present your viewpoint.

items.meaning: Introducing a personal observation or conclusion, often with a softening effect.
items.example: It seems to me that we're overlooking a crucial detail in the plan.
items.plain: I think we're overlooking a crucial detail in the plan.
items.note: A polite and less assertive way to offer an opinion.

items.meaning: Expressing a tendency or willingness to concur with someone.
items.example: Given the new data, I'm inclined to agree with your assessment.
items.plain: Given the new data, I tend to agree with your assessment.
items.note: A polite and slightly formal way to express agreement.

items.meaning: Expressing polite disagreement or hesitation to concur.
items.example: I'm not sure I agree with that approach, considering the potential risks.
items.plain: I don't know if I agree with that approach, considering the potential risks.
items.note: A polite and softened way to express disagreement.

items.meaning: Politely expressing an intention to question or dispute a statement.
items.example: With respect, I'd like to challenge that assumption about market growth.
items.plain: Respectfully, I want to question that assumption about market growth.
items.note: A formal and assertive way to express disagreement or doubt.

items.text: Could you clarify what you mean
items.form: Could you clarify what you mean
items.meaning: Politely asking for a more precise explanation of a statement.
items.example: I'm a bit confused; could you clarify what you mean by "streamlining operations"?
items.plain: I'm confused; can you explain what you mean by "streamlining operations"?
items.note: A common and polite request for a clearer explanation.

items.meaning: Introducing a more detailed or precise explanation.
items.example: To be more specific, we need to reduce costs by fifteen percent.
items.plain: More precisely, we need to reduce costs by fifteen percent.
items.note: Used when you want to add detail or narrow down a general statement.

items.meaning: Introducing a point or piece of information one wishes to share.
items.example: Before we finish, I wanted to mention that the report is due next week.
items.plain: Before we finish, I wanted to say that the report is due next week.
items.note: A polite way to introduce a new, often important, piece of information.

items.meaning: Introducing a brief remark or piece of information.
items.example: Just a quick point: we should also consider the environmental impact.
items.plain: I have a brief comment: we should also consider the environmental impact.
items.note: Used to interject a short, often additional, thought.

items.meaning: Expressing a desire to contribute one's opinion to a discussion.
items.example: If there's a moment, I'd like to weigh in on the marketing strategy.
items.plain: If there's a moment, I want to share my opinion on the marketing strategy.
items.note: A common, slightly informal way to offer your contribution.

items.text: I'm not sure I caught that
items.form: I'm not sure I caught that
items.meaning: Politely indicating that one did not hear or understand something.
items.example: Sorry, I'm not sure I caught that last part; could you repeat it?
items.plain: Sorry, I didn't hear that last part; could you repeat it?
items.note: A polite way to ask for repetition, often implying a technical issue or distraction.

items.text: Could you run that by me again
items.form: Could you run that by me again
items.meaning: Politely asking for something to be repeated or re-explained.
items.example: I was distracted for a second; could you run that by me again?
items.plain: I was distracted; can you repeat that for me?
items.note: A common and informal way to ask for repetition or clarification.

items.meaning: Expressing significant difficulty in comprehending something.
items.example: I'm struggling to understand the rationale behind this sudden change.
items.plain: I'm having a lot of difficulty understanding why this change happened so suddenly.
items.note: A more emphatic way to express confusion than "I'm not clear."

items.text: I'd like to get your input
items.form: I'd like to get your input
items.meaning: Politely asking for someone's contribution, opinions, or advice.
items.example: Before we finalize, I'd like to get your input on the design options.
items.plain: Before we finalize, I want your opinions on the design options.
items.note: A professional way to solicit contributions from others.

items.meaning: Asking for someone's viewpoint or way of looking at a situation.
items.example: We've heard from the team, but what's your perspective on the challenges?
items.plain: We've heard from the team, but what is your view on the challenges?
items.note: A polite way to ask for an individual's unique viewpoint.

items.meaning: Expressing an interest in learning more about a specific topic.
items.example: I'm curious about the potential impact of this decision on our partners.
items.plain: I want to know more about the potential impact of this decision on our partners.
items.note: A polite and engaging way to ask for more information.

items.meaning: Expressing a desire for additional information or elaboration.
items.example: That sounds promising; I'd like to hear more about the project details.
items.plain: That sounds promising; I want to hear more about the project details.
items.note: A polite way to encourage someone to continue explaining.

items.meaning: Introducing an even more detailed explanation than before.
items.example: To elaborate further, we've conducted extensive market research.
items.plain: To give even more details, we've conducted extensive market research.
items.note: Used when you need to provide additional depth to a previous explanation.

items.meaning: Expressing polite skepticism or a lack of full belief in an argument.
items.example: I'm not quite convinced by the proposed timeline; it seems too ambitious.
items.plain: I don't fully believe the proposed timeline; it seems too ambitious.
items.note: A polite and diplomatic way to express doubt or disagreement.

items.text: I'd like to raise a point
items.form: I'd like to raise a point
items.meaning: Politely introducing a new topic or an important consideration.
items.example: Before we move on, I'd like to raise a point about the budget allocation.
items.plain: Before we move on, I want to bring up a topic about the budget allocation.
items.note: A formal way to introduce a new item for discussion.

items.meaning: Politely asking for a repetition of an explanation.
items.example: I apologize, but I missed that; could you explain that again?
items.plain: Sorry, I missed that; can you explain it once more?
items.note: A direct and polite request for re-explanation.

items.text: I'm not sure I'm explaining myself
items.form: I'm not sure I'm explaining myself
items.meaning: Expressing doubt about the clarity of one's own communication.
items.example: I'm not sure I'm explaining myself well, but I hope you understand my concern.
items.plain: I don't know if I'm being clear, but I hope you understand my concern.
items.note: Used when you feel your message might not be coming across clearly.

items.meaning: Stating an intention to re-explain or re-attempt something.
items.example: That didn't come out right; let me try again to articulate my thoughts.
items.plain: That wasn't clear; I'll try to explain my thoughts differently.
items.note: A simple and direct way to indicate a second attempt at communication.

items.text: Our time is drawing to a close
items.form: Our time is drawing to a close
items.meaning: Informing participants that the scheduled duration of the call is nearly over.
items.example: Our time is drawing to a close, so let's quickly summarize our action points.
items.plain: Our time is nearly finished, so let's quickly summarize our action points.
items.note: A formal way to signal the need to conclude a meeting.

items.text: I think we've covered the main points
items.form: I think we've covered the main points
items.meaning: Expressing the belief that all essential topics have been discussed.
items.example: I think we've covered the main points for today's agenda.
items.plain: I believe we have discussed all the important topics for today's agenda.
items.note: Used to signal readiness to conclude a discussion.

items.meaning: Introducing the final remarks or summary of a conversation.
items.example: To conclude our discussion, I'll send out the meeting minutes by tomorrow.
items.plain: To end our discussion, I'll send out the meeting minutes by tomorrow.
items.note: A formal way to transition to the end of a conversation.

items.meaning: Stating an intention to send an email summarizing or continuing the discussion.
items.example: I'll send a follow-up email with all the agreed-upon action items.
items.plain: I will send an email later with all the agreed-upon action items.
items.note: A common professional commitment for post-call communication.

items.meaning: Suggesting to arrange another meeting or call to continue a topic.
items.example: We couldn't cover everything, so let's schedule a follow-up for next week.
items.plain: We didn't finish everything, so let's arrange another meeting for next week.
items.note: Used when more discussion is needed on a topic.

items.meaning: Stating an intention to distribute a list of tasks agreed upon during the call.
items.example: After this call, I'll circulate the action points to everyone involved.
items.plain: After this call, I will send the list of tasks to everyone involved.
items.note: A common professional commitment for distributing meeting outcomes.

items.meaning: A friendly way to express enjoyment of the conversation, especially with someone known.
items.example: Thanks for your time, Sarah; it was good catching up with you.
items.plain: Thanks for your time, Sarah; I enjoyed talking with you.
items.note: Informal and friendly, suitable for colleagues or acquaintances.

items.meaning: Stating an intention to transmit relevant documents or resources.
items.example: As discussed, I'll send you the materials for the upcoming workshop.
items.plain: As discussed, I will send you the documents for the upcoming workshop.
items.note: A common commitment to share resources after a discussion.

items.meaning: Stating an intention to verify the details of a future appointment.
items.example: Before the end of the day, I'll confirm our next meeting time and agenda.
items.plain: Before the end of the day, I will verify the details of our next meeting.
items.note: A professional commitment to finalize future arrangements.

items.meaning: Stating an intention to send a brief written message.
items.example: I'll send a quick note to everyone summarizing our decisions.
items.plain: I will send a short message to everyone summarizing our decisions.
items.note: A less formal alternative to "send an email," implying brevity.

items.meaning: Stating an intention to provide a web address for information or resources.
items.example: I'll send you the link to the shared drive where all documents are stored.
items.plain: I will send you the web address for the shared drive with all documents.
items.note: A common commitment to share digital resources.

items.meaning: Stating an intention to transmit a specific written file.
items.example: I'll send you the document with the revised proposal by end of day.
items.plain: I will transmit the file with the revised proposal to you by end of day.
items.note: A direct commitment to share a specific file.

items.meaning: Stating an intention to transmit a formal written account of findings.
items.example: Once it's finalized, I'll send you the report on the quarterly sales figures.
items.plain: Once it's finalized, I will transmit the sales figures report to you.
items.note: A common commitment to share a formal report.

items.meaning: Stating the reason for a call is to reply to a previous communication.
items.example: I'm calling in response to your email about the project timeline.
items.plain: I am calling because of your email about the project timeline.
items.note: A formal and clear way to state the purpose of your call.

items.meaning: Stating the purpose of a call is to talk about a specific topic.
items.example: I'm calling to discuss the upcoming changes to the company policy.
items.plain: I am calling to talk about the upcoming changes to the company policy.
items.note: A direct and professional way to state the call's objective.

items.text: I'm calling to provide an update
items.form: I'm calling to provide an update
items.meaning: Stating the purpose of a call is to give current information.
items.example: I'm calling to provide an update on the status of your application.
items.plain: I am calling to give you current information on your application's status.
items.note: A professional way to initiate a call with new information.

items.meaning: Stating the purpose of a call is to arrange an appointment or event.
items.example: I'm calling to schedule a meeting regarding the new client proposal.
items.plain: I am calling to arrange a meeting about the new client proposal.
items.note: A common and direct way to state the purpose of arranging something.

items.meaning: Stating the purpose of a call is to verify that something has been received.
items.example: I'm calling to confirm receipt of the documents you sent yesterday.
items.plain: I am calling to verify that I received the documents you sent yesterday.
items.note: A formal and precise way to confirm delivery of items.
